The absence of classic CF features (e.g., pancreatic insufficiency, nasal polyps, sinusitis, childhood ear infections, failure to thrive) makes CF less likely — but *not excluded*, as atypical/late-onset CF can present with isolated bronchiectasis. Alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency typically presents with early-onset emphysema (not bronchiectasis-predominant disease) and is less consistent with preserved FEV1/FVC and dominant bronchial infection. Critically, HRCT chest — the definitive imaging test for bronchiectasis — is *pending*, and no structural confirmation yet exists.
